title: Reading Comprehension Foundation
tagline: Year 2 — Reading a short passage and answering factual, vocabulary, inference and main-idea questions

introduction.overview: Reading comprehension (RC) tests whether you can understand a passage and answer questions about it. Question types are factual (what the passage says), vocabulary-in-context (what a word means here), inference (what must be true because of what is said), main idea (what the passage is mostly about) and tone or purpose. At this level the passages are short, and the answers can be checked against the text. The golden rule: answer from the passage, not from your own opinion.
introduction.placementRelevance: Reading comprehension is commonly asked in the verbal ability section of company aptitude rounds, and it is the most heavily weighted verbal skill because it reflects real reading ability.
introduction.realWorldContext: Understanding emails, reports and instructions quickly and accurately depends on the same skills.

learningObjectives: Identify the main idea of a passage
Infer meanings from context and from what is stated
Recognise the author's tone and purpose
Eliminate options that go beyond the passage

prerequisiteKnowledge.quickRefresher: A passage has a main idea, supporting details and a tone. Signal words (however, therefore, on the other hand) show how ideas are related.

coreDefinitions: Main idea: the central point of the passage.
Supporting detail: a fact or example that supports the main idea.
Inference: a conclusion that must follow from what is stated, but is not stated directly.
Vocabulary in context: the meaning of a word as used in the passage.
Tone: the author's attitude (admiring, critical, neutral, worried).
conceptExplanation.theoreticalIntuition: The passage contains every answer you need. Read once for the main idea, then use the question to look back for the evidence. If you cannot point to a line that supports an option, the option is not safe.
conceptExplanation.visualOrMentalModel: Read the passage and summarise it in one line. For each question, find the line that supports the answer. For inference, ask "what must be true?"; for vocabulary, test the word in the sentence.

importantRulesAndFormulas.title: Main idea check
importantRulesAndFormulas.formula: The correct option covers the whole passage, not just one detail
importantRulesAndFormulas.description: Reject too narrow and too broad options.

importantRulesAndFormulas.title: Fact check
importantRulesAndFormulas.formula: Find the line that states it

importantRulesAndFormulas.title: Inference check
importantRulesAndFormulas.formula: It must be true given the passage

importantRulesAndFormulas.title: Vocabulary check
importantRulesAndFormulas.formula: Substitute the meaning into the sentence

importantRulesAndFormulas.title: Extreme-word filter
importantRulesAndFormulas.formula: Reject options with always, never, all, only unless the passage uses them

mainNarrative: Read the passage once, quickly, for its structure. In the passage about Rahul, the idea is that Rahul was determined to study despite the distance. The main details are the distance (five kilometres), his routine and his teachers' admiration.
For factual questions, scan for the key words of the question. "How far was the nearest school?" points to "five kilometres". Do not rely on memory; check the line.
For vocabulary questions, substitute each option into the sentence. "Rahul, however, was determined" contrasts with children who gave up, so determined means firm in purpose.

For inference questions, choose the option that must be true. "Students who sleep less than six hours often find it hard to concentrate" lets us infer that a student who sleeps only four hours is likely to find it hard to concentrate.

For main idea and tone questions, avoid options that are too narrow (one detail) or too broad (beyond the passage). For the factory passage the main idea is the conflict between economic benefit and environmental damage.

deepDiveAspects.title: Passage structure
deepDiveAspects.content: Many passages follow: idea, problem, response. Signal words such as however and therefore mark the turns.

deepDiveAspects.title: Reading speed
deepDiveAspects.content: Aim to read at a steady pace and use the questions as a guide. Rereading the whole passage for every question wastes time.

solvedExamples.title: Factual
solvedExamples.question:
Passage: Rahul's village had no school. Children had to walk five kilometres to the nearest town to study. Many gave up after the primary classes. Rahul, however, was determined. He woke up at five every day, walked to school, and returned home in the evening to help his father on the farm. His teachers admired his dedication.

How far did the children have to walk to study?

steps.title: Scan for the key words
steps.explanation: The question asks about distance to school.

solvedExamples.title: Vocabulary in context
solvedExamples.question:
Passage: Rahul's village had no school. Children had to walk five kilometres to the nearest town to study. Many gave up after the primary classes. Rahul, however, was determined. He woke up at five every day, walked to school, and returned home in the evening to help his father on the farm. His teachers admired his dedication.

In the passage, the word "determined" means

steps.title: Contrast
steps.explanation: Many gave up; Rahul was determined.

solvedExamples.title: Inference
solvedExamples.question:
Passage: Sleep is as important as food for health. During sleep the body repairs itself and the brain stores what was learned during the day. Students who sleep less than six hours often find it hard to concentrate. Doctors recommend seven to eight hours of sleep for most adults.

A student who sleeps only four hours a night is most likely to

steps.title: Evidence
steps.explanation: Less than six hours → hard to concentrate.

solvedExamples.whyItWorks: The passage links short sleep to poor concentration.

traditionalVsShortcut.traditionalMethod: Rely on memory and general knowledge.
traditionalVsShortcut.shortcutMethod: Summarise the passage in one line, then for each question find the line that supports the answer and reject extreme options.

placementTips.eliminationTechnique: Eliminate options that contradict a line in the passage.
placementTips.questionSelectionAdvice: Read the questions first on long passages.
placementTips.recruiterInsight: Wrong options are usually partly true but not supported.

selfCheckQuestions: Can I state the main idea in one line?
Can I find a fact quickly?
Can I make a safe inference?
